texts.preamble: Western India C. Brnads Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2024
texts.facts: 2. Although notice has been issued to the opposite party no.2 and the same has been served, which is apparent from the office report, but till today none appeared on behalf of the opposite party no.2. No counter affidavit has been preferred on behalf of the State as well as on behalf of opposite party no.2. 3. The applicant, through the present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. have invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court with the prayer that the proceedings of Complaint Case No.2062 Western India C. Brnads Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94646456/ 1 of 2000 (State of U.P. Versus Babu Lal Gupta & Another), under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 2/2000, P.S. Kotra Bazar, District Jalaun, pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jalaun at Orai be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 4. It is the case of the applicant that the opposite party no.2 filed a false and frivolous complaint case in District Jalaun against the applicant, whereupon only considering the statements of complainant and witnesses recorded under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C., learned Judicial Magistrate, Jalaun at Orai vide its order dated 07.09.2000, summoned the applicant without complying the mandatory provisions of Section 202 (1) Cr.P.C., since the applicant is resident of other districts.
texts.arguments: 5. Sri Ajay Sengar, learned counsel for the applicant, at the very outset, submitted that the summoning order, which has been put under challenge through the instant application is in non-compliance of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C., wherein it has been mentioned that if the summoning order has to be issued beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the concerned magistrate, the mandatory provision for inquiry is to be directed first and then after receiving the report, the summoning order may be issued. 7. However, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer as made in the instant application and rebutted the stand taken up by the learned counsel for the applicant but did not dispute the provisions of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C. 8.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 5. Sri Ajay Sengar, learned counsel for the applicant, at the very outset, submitted that the summoning order, which has been put under challenge through the instant application is in non-compliance of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C., wherein it has been mentioned that if the summoning order has to be issued beyond the territorial jurisdiction of the concerned magistrate, the mandatory provision for inquiry is to be directed first and then after receiving the report, the summoning order may be issued. 7. However, learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the prayer as made in the instant application and rebutted the stand taken up by the learned counsel for the applicant but did not dispute the provisions of Section 202 (1) of Cr.P.C. 8.
